audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers handed Lucian five of seven stages in a matchup he wins 34.38% of, and the same page's whys[3..6] say Malphite owns everything from 4-5 onward. The packet chart and the mirror both read Skill, Lucian, Skill, Malphite, Malphite, Malphite, Malphite. The header was also incoherent: diff HARD, the yellow even-tone, diffRating 5.5/10 and two rating lines saying 'Even matchup'.
audit.why: Malphite's armour stacking directly counters an all-physical kit, and Unstoppable Force is a point-and-click engage that Relentless Pursuit cannot answer. Only level 2 — before Thunderclap's armour and the Q slow scale — is genuinely Lucian's.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 set to Skill, Skill, Malphite, Malphite, Malphite, Malphite in both layers as matched pairs (row 1 stays Lucian), ratings re-scaled to 5/7/5/3/2/3/2, and the header restated as a hard 7.5/10 matchup with the orange tone.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4] described level 6 as Lucian's ult spike ('lane-clear and execute chip') on the level Malphite takes the lane, and no cooldown appeared on the chart at all.
audit.why: Unstoppable Force is 130/115/100s at 1000 range and knocks up; it ignores Relentless Pursuit entirely because it is a point-and-click dash onto you, not a skillshot you can sidestep.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now names Unstoppable Force and its 130s rank-1 cooldown as the reason not to step up; report[5].t carries the same number.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags that this matchup never names a single Malphite ability. Three real interactions were absent: Ground Slam grounds Relentless Pursuit, Granite Shield absorbs up to 10% of his max health before your burst starts counting, and Thunderclap is an auto reset that also applies on-hit.
audit.why: Ground Slam is a flat 7s with the grounding flag — Lucian's exit is his dash, so a grounded Lucian in a tank's face is simply dead, and that is the single most decision-relevant fact in the lane. Granite Shield means the first tenth of his HP bar is free for him, so a burst window opened before it is chipped off does nothing. Riot's Thunderclap text: his attacks create aftershocks — the wind-up is the tell.
audit.corrected: Ground Slam's grounding and its 7s cooldown written into phases[3].why and report[5].t (matching the mirror's finding from the other side), Granite Shield's 10% absorb into dontsFull[0].d, Thunderclap's auto reset and 400 range into dosFull[2].d.

edits.before: Passive double-shots win level 1 outright — Q through the wave on his last-hits and weave doubletaps on every step-up.
edits.after: Both level 1s are weak, but Seismic Shard already pokes and steals move speed — last-hit at range and set up your 2.

edits.before: Full kit: Q-AA-E-AA-W-AA strings chunk a third of his HP. Trade on every CS he takes from the wrong angle.
edits.after: His Q slow neuters your kiting and Thunderclap's armour blunts your shots — the lane levels out here.

edits.before: Keep the pressure rolling but track Unstoppable Force — your lead is HP-bar bullying, not all-in math, until items arrive.
edits.after: Ground Slam grounds Relentless Pursuit on a flat 7s, and his armour shrugs off poke while Q chip drains your mana.

edits.before: The Culling adds lane-clear and execute chip — use it through walls on recalls and low-HP escapes.
edits.after: Unstoppable Force is a 130s point-and-click engage your E cannot answer — never step up while it is up.

edits.before: First item spike is your kill window — the dash-weave combo now deletes half bars. Force the issue before he stabilizes.
edits.after: Stacked armour makes physical Lightslinger and Culling barely register, and his Q keeps you slowed and walled off.

edits.before: You fall off relative to top-lane scalers — convert the lead into towers and roams before the 3-item brawlers arrive.
edits.after: Two armour items plus his teamfight R make you irrelevant in the duel — concede it and play the map instead.

edits.before: Track Malphite’s Unstoppable Force: Unstoppable engage — usually banked for teamfights, punish lane passivity. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Unstoppable Force is 130s at rank 1 — commit only on its downtime. Ground Slam grounds Relentless Pursuit on a flat 7s, so bait the slam before you dash.

edits.before: Malphite spends Unstoppable Force early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Thunderclap is an auto reset — its wind-up, not the cast, is your cue to be outside 400.

edits.before: That’s Malphite’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Granite Shield eats up to 10% of his max HP — chip it off before you commit.

notes: The two layers AGREED with each other here and were both wrong — every structural gate that compares full to content would have passed this page while it told a Lucian player he wins levels 1, 3, 6 and two-items against a Malphite he beats a third of the time. The only signal that caught it was the content whys sitting directly under the chart and saying the opposite. Worth noting for the regression tooling: whys[N] vs win[N] agreement is a check that does not exist yet and would have caught karma, kassadin, kled, ksante, lillia and malphite in this slice alone.
